summary.headline: Q4 FY26 sales rose 21% to INR706 crore and FY26 PBT hit a record INR356 crore, but management flags 18-20% EBITDA as sustainable, not the 21.7% delivered.
summary.overview: Q4 FY26 sales were INR706 crore versus INR583 crore a year earlier, with raw material-to-sales falling to 50.06% from 56.35%. FY26 EBITDA was INR388 crore (21.7% of total income) and PBT INR356 crore (19.6%), supported by in-house backward integration and a selective order-acceptance stance. The unexecuted order board rose 15% to INR1,863 crore as of April 1, 2026, including Precision Components, and the company remains debt-free with about INR460 crore net cash. Management called FY26's margin an exception and guided to 18-20% EBITDA going forward, while reaffirming a 20%+ growth aspiration.

financial_highlights.change: vs INR588 crore in Q4 FY25

financial_highlights.value: 600% of face value (INR12 per share), including final of INR8.50 and interim of INR3.50
About INR460 crore as on April 1, 2026

segments.name: Compression (only reportable segment)
segments.commentary: Accounts for about 93.4% of total income; segment operating profit margin was 24.9% in FY26 versus 21.7% in FY25. Management said Q4 margin was a one-off and sustainable range is 18-20%.

segments.name: Air compression / ACD
segments.commentary: Roughly 18-20% of business. Tezcatlipoca centrifugal compressors gaining share (about 130 machines in field, 85 commissioned); reciprocating gas compressor orders at record highs; screw compressors lagged.

segments.name: Refrigeration (KC/KCX, Khione)
segments.commentary: Roughly 40-45% of business. Record KC/KCX volumes in FY26 and several large packages executed, some in Q4; Khione sales picking up.

segments.name: Process Gas Systems (PGS)
segments.commentary: Roughly 35-40% of business. Management described FY26 as lagging in oil and gas due to slower order finalisation; O&M base spans over 1,000 CNG stations; CNG order activity picking up in Q4.

segments.name: Precision Engineering (non-reportable in FY26)
segments.commentary: New division using Nashik and Hadapsar forgings, castings and machined components. Part of the INR1,863 crore order board; about INR500 crore executable beyond FY27. Will be reportable from Q1 FY27 per management.

guidance_outlook: EBITDA margin: 18-20% is the sustainable range; FY26's 21.7% is described as an exception, though management said it could reach 21% in good quarters.
Growth aspiration of 20%+ on top line and bottom line over a long period; management said it expects to deliver sales above order board conversion and reach 20%+ in FY27.
Equipment business (short-cycle, 4-12 weeks) targeted at 20-25% of revenue; new products targeted at 10-15% of sales.
Zephyros air conditioning package to be commercialised in Q1 FY27; A-800 centrifugal frame launch expected in about one month.
Capex of INR320 crore is a PLI commitment, of which about INR60 crore spent; balance to be incurred over about 2 years.
Board approved sub-division of equity shares from INR2 face value to INR1, subject to shareholder approval.
capex_capacity: Tezcatlipoca incremental capacity installed and commissioned; available from Q1 FY27.
INR320 crore PLI-linked capex, of which roughly INR60 crore incurred, covering backward integration in motors, heat exchangers and sheet metal for Zephyros at Saswad and Nashik.
Backward integration at Nashik feeding Hadapsar (air compressor and PED) and Saswad; this drove lower raw material cost ratio.
Continued capex to support growth and PLI-linked new product development; depreciation rose to INR31.1 crore in FY26 from INR28.9 crore.
Management said capacity is not a constraint at present; a subsidiary is being restructured and will take time to turn positive.
demand_pricing: Unexecuted order board INR1,863 crore as of April 1, 2026, up 15% from INR1,624 crore a year earlier; includes Precision Components. About INR500 crore executable beyond FY27.
Order inflow in the last two quarters about INR650 crore (per analyst); the order book is skewed toward products, which management said should shorten execution cycles.
Export about 6% of sales; MENA was a large share earlier but is slowing due to the Middle East conflict, with focus shifting to Southeast Asia and North Africa.
Management said price increases are passed to customers on short-cycle work, and large packages have had vendor pricing finalised, so no direct margin hit expected.
Gas package competition: specified vendor lists and lower-cost competitors make cost innovation difficult in Middle East gas packages.

qa_highlights.question: What is the executable order book and what is the Precision Engineering share?
qa_highlights.answer: Ramesh Birajdar said the INR1,863 crore book includes Precision Components; about INR500 crore is executable beyond FY27, and the equipment business brings in INR600-700 crore a year that is executed and dispatched within the year.

qa_highlights.question: Zephyros go-to-market and returns on the INR320 crore capex?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said the target markets are small machine shops, restaurants and banquet halls, with channel build-out via dealers. Margins will be below the 25-30% sought, and returns will come from volume; INR60 crore has been spent so far.

qa_highlights.question: Middle East exposure and ability to win gas packages?
qa_highlights.answer: Aman Kirloskar said the Middle East is a key market for packages but is not a large share of total business; near-term dispatch and new orders are difficult, and the company has won Middle East packages before.

qa_highlights.question: Why did FY26 growth not follow a book-to-bill near 1 last year, and what changes now?
qa_highlights.answer: Management blamed reliance on the gas business, where growth has been difficult, and said actions are being taken to improve competitiveness. Equipment and Precision Engineering are expected to carry growth in FY27.

qa_highlights.question: Is 21.5-21.7% EBITDA sustainable versus the 18-20% guidance?
qa_highlights.answer: Aman Kirloskar said investors should not judge quarter to quarter; 18-20% is the base, with 21% possible. Ramesh Birajdar said Q4 gross margin crossed about 23% but 18-20% remains the sustainable core-business range.

qa_highlights.question: What drives the CNG and CGD demand outlook?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said daughter stations are about 70% of new stations, with mother stations needed for long-haul supply, and demand should rise for both over time. Ramesh Birajdar pointed to ONGC's about INR200 billion investment over five to six years as an opportunity.

risks_watch: Margin normalisation: management guided to 18-20% EBITDA after a 21.7% FY26; watch whether Q1 FY27 holds above 20%.
Gas segment growth has been weak; PGS is 35-40% of business and CNG/PGS order conversion needs to show.
Precision Engineering order sustainability is unclear; management declined to give a backlog split or say whether INR500 crore inflows will repeat.
Middle East conflict is slowing dispatches and new export gas orders, with MENA share of exports falling.
Zephyros commercial launch in Q1 FY27 with unproven demand; a subsidiary restructuring is under way with no timeline for positive results.
Equity sub-division from INR2 to INR1 face value and final dividend are subject to shareholder approval.
summary.management_tone: Confident on the long-term story and order board growth, but cautious on margins, explicitly guiding down to 18-20% EBITDA. Evasive on Precision Engineering sustainability, backlog split and the subsidiary's timeline, and on gas-segment growth, which management called a difficulty.
key_quotes: While this quarter and year has been good on the margin front, we would like to caution that this year would be a bit of an exception, a margin expectation of 18% to 20% EBITDA would be more sustainable.
With our strong order board and a substantial volume of active proposals entering the new financial year, we are confident in achieving our growth objective of 20% plus.
So we generally don't give a breakup of segments.
